title: POC scoping - workload & traffic model for Emerald Lending
summary: Discovery and POC scoping focused on modeling Emerald Lending's inference workload. Customer provided traffic shape and token distributions for their summarization and extraction flows. Discussed success criteria (latency and quality), target QPS/concurrency for POC, benchmark plan (synthetic and replay), and pilot timeline (2 weeks of staging tests + 4 week evaluation). Action items: Redwood to share model catalog, pricing and pilot runbook; customer to provide anonymized sample payloads and request logs; schedule benchmark run next Tuesday.
next_steps: Redwood: Share model catalog, quantization recommendations, and pricing sheet by 2027-03-08
Customer: Provide 7 days of anonymized request logs and sample payloads by 2027-03-07
Schedule benchmark run (synthetic + replay) for 2027-03-09, 10:00 AM PT
Set up pilot environment (dedicated or hosted) and test service account access by 2027-03-11
Follow-up call to review benchmark results 2027-03-12
action_items: Samira Patel (Redwood) - Send model catalog + recommended configs (quantization, batching) - due 2027-03-08
Derek Huang (Redwood) - Prepare benchmark runbook and synthetic traffic harness - due 2027-03-09
Marta Ruiz (Emerald) - Export 7 days of anonymized request logs + sample payloads - due 2027-03-07
Tom Everett (Emerald) - Provision test VPC peering/access or API keys for pilot - due 2027-03-11
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-05 14:00 PT | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Derek (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood SE), Marta (Emerald Head of ML), Tom (Platform Lead), Priya (DevOps), Evan (Product)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're here to scope the POC around workload and traffic modeling for Emerald Lending. Quick intros?
[00:10] Marta: Hi, Marta here. I run ML at Emerald. We're trying to replace a mix of rules + smaller models with a single summarization + extraction pipeline.
[00:18] Tom: Tom, infra lead. I'll own the pilot infra and networking.
[00:22] Priya: Priya, DevOps. I'll help with access and logs.
[00:26] Evan: Evan, PM. I'll define success criteria from product side.
[00:30] Samira: Great. Derek, Lina, want to quick overview?
[00:34] Derek: Yeah hi, Derek from Redwood. We'll help model traffic, run benchmarks, and propose dedicated vs hosted options. We typically break workload into QPS, concurrency, and token distributions.
[01:02] Lina: And also discuss caching, KV cache behavior, prefix caching and potential quantization to reduce cost.
[01:18] Marta: Cool. To be concrete, current production traffic is about 6 QPS average, spikes to ~55 QPS during batch windows. Most requests are user-submitted doc summarize + entity extraction. Typical input lengths are 50-250 tokens, outputs 30-150 tokens.
[01:40] Derek: Helpful. Do you have percentiles for input length? Median, p95?
[01:46] Marta: Median input ~72 tokens, p90 ~180, p99 ~420. Outputs median 90, p90 140.
[01:56] Samira: Great—so for POC we should model both the median and the tail. Are there long-running sessions or chat-like flows?
[02:06] Marta: Mostly stateless requests, few sessions. We do have a small conversational assistant internally but that's not the first POC.
[02:16] Tom: On infra, we currently run VMs on GCP with a private VPC. For POC we prefer Redwood Dedicated but we can do hosted if initial benchmarks look good. Security is important: SOC2, SSO, audit logs.
[02:34] Samira: Understood. We'll share SOC2 docs and our private deployment options. For the workload: what's your latency SLO?
[02:42] Evan: Product desires p50 < 700ms for the summary call (average 100 output tokens), p95 < 2s. Cost targets are more flexible but we'd like to keep per-response cost predictable.
[02:56] Derek: Those are reasonable for optimized models with batching and prefix caching. For planning, can you confirm concurrency at peak?
[03:06] Marta: Peak concurrency we see up to 40 concurrent active requests during spike windows. Sustained concurrency usually 8-12.
[03:14] Lina: OK so POC target: emulate median traffic at 8 QPS with bursts to 60 QPS and concurrency up to 40. We'll run both synthetic steady-state and replay from logs.
[03:28] Priya: We can export the request logs but will strip PII. Format is JSON lines with request_id, input_length_tokens, response_length_tokens, timestamp, and latency.
[03:40] Derek: Perfect. For benchmarks we'll need a small sample of those plus a distribution for inter-arrival times. We'll run two types of workloads: 1) Synthetic mix (70% summaries, 30% extraction) shaped to your QPS and token distributions; 2) Replay exact timestamps from logs to capture burstiness.
[04:02] Samira: On model selection: do you have preferences? We can test a smaller fast model for latency and a larger for quality. We recommend testing: redwood-llama-13b-qlora (quantized) and an open LLM we verify for accuracy on your eval set.
[04:20] Marta: We need to ensure extraction quality doesn't degrade. We'll supply 100 eval prompts and expected outputs for quality gating.
[04:28] Derek: Good. Success criteria we propose combining latency and quality: quality regression < 2% on F1 for extraction OR manual QA pass; and latency p50/p95 under your thresholds. If both meet, we consider pilot successful.
[04:44] Evan: That sounds right. Also include cost per 1k requests as a metric so finance can sign off.
[04:51] Samira: We'll include cost modeling with token breakdown and batching effects.
[05:00] [05:00] Tom: Quick question on KV caching — we have many repeated prefixes because users upload same doc templates. How does Redwood handle prefix caching?
[05:10] Derek: Redwood's runtime supports prefix/KV caching and we can configure cache TTL. Hits can drastically reduce compute. In our benchmarks we'll run both cold and warm cache scenarios.
[05:22] Priya: Network: for dedicated we'd want VPC peering; for hosted we'll need private link if possible. Docs?
[05:30] Samira: We'll send VPC peering docs and our private deployment checklist.
[05:36] Marta: For the POC data controls: we need encryption at rest KMS, audit logs to S3 for 90 days, and RBAC.
[05:46] Lina: Redwood supports KMS integrations and can forward audit logs; we'll include retention configs in the runbook.
[05:54] Derek: Benchmark plan outline: 1) Stage environment deploy with same model/quant config; 2) Run synthetic steady-state 1 hour at 8 QPS; 3) Run burst test 5 min bursts to 60 QPS; 4) Run replay of 7-day sample at real timestamps; 5) Measure latency, throughput, token/sec, GPU utilization, and cost.
[06:18] Evan: How long will this take?
[06:21] Samira: We can execute benchmarks in ~2 working days once we have logs and test access. Pilot staging + validation 2 weeks, then 4 weeks evaluation. So overall ~6 weeks to decision if everything moves fast.
[06:36] Marta: Sounds fine. For quality gating, we'll want automatic evals after each run and a manual spot-check for extraction edge cases.
[06:46] Derek: We'll integrate with your eval harness. For replay we need to make sure timestamps don't exceed token quotas — we can throttle to match your profile.
[06:58] Tom: What about concurrency limits and autoscale? If we hit sustained 60 QPS, do you autoscale GPU pool?
[07:05] Derek: In Dedicated we can configure autoscaler with burst capacity. For hosted, we have multi-tenant pools and fallback policies. We'll document latencies under both modes.
[07:18] Samira: Let's nail down the POC traffic numbers to record in the runbook. From what we heard: median QPS 6-8, typical concurrency 8-12, peak bursts to 55-60 QPS, peak concurrency up to 40, median input tokens 72, median output tokens 90, p95 input 180, p99 420. We'll use synthetic mix: 70% summary, 30% extraction.
[07:44] Marta: Correct. Also include edge-case long docs (2k tokens) but those are <0.5% of traffic.
[07:52] Lina: We'll add a tail workload to stress memory and KV cache.
[07:58] Evan: Any regulatory hold-ups? We need to keep logs for audit and ensure data residency in US.
[08:06] Samira: Redwood has US region deployments and can keep data in customer region for Private/Dedicated. We'll include residency options in the docs.
[08:16] Priya: For the replay we'll sanitize fields. How do we feed the inputs? S3? Or direct POST replay?
[08:22] Derek: Either works. For high-fidelity replay we usually do direct POSTs from a harness; for easier setup, S3 with a worker that reads and replays is fine. We'll provide harness code snippets.
[08:34] Marta: For measurement we want p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU token/sec, cost per 1k requests, and quality F1 for extraction.
[08:44] Samira: Noted. Any blockers?
[08:46] Tom: We need Redwood to send security and VPC docs and a checklist for pilot onboarding.
[08:52] Samira: We'll send those plus the model catalog and recommended configs.
[08:56] Evan: One more — benchmarks should include both quantized and non-quantized models to compare quality vs latency/cost tradeoffs.
[09:03] Derek: Absolutely. We'll run q4_0 and int8 quant variants where available.
[09:08] Samira: Ok wrap-up. Recap next steps and owners?
[09:12] Lina: I'll own the runbook and benchmarks. Samira will own pricing and model catalog. Marta and Tom to provide logs + access.
[09:22] Marta: We'll aim to get logs by Monday and provision test access.
[09:26] Samira: Great. We'll schedule the benchmark run for Tuesday at 10 AM PT and follow up after results. Thanks everyone.

[52:00] Meeting end.
